enriched_description: Small cylindrical container designed for pharmaceutical storage, typically 30-120 ml capacity. Constructed from opaque or translucent plastic (amber, white, or orange) with a screw-on or snap-on child-resistant cap. Cap features a push-and-turn mechanism or ribbed grip texture for secure closure. Body is smooth cylindrical with a flat base for upright stability. Exterior surface bears printed or adhesive label containing dosage information, drug name, and pharmacy details. Dimensions approximately 4-8 cm in height and 3-5 cm in diameter. Distinguishing features include pharmaceutical labeling, child-resistant closure mechanism, and standardized small cylindrical proportions.

Rectangular or square cushion designed to support the head during sleep, typically 50 x 75 cm in standard size. Outer casing constructed from woven cotton, polyester, or blended fabric with smooth or textured weave pattern. Filling consists of down feathers, synthetic fiberfill, memory foam, or buckwheat hulls, creating a soft, compressible form. Surface exhibits slight wrinkling from use, with visible seams along edges. Closure may be envelope-style or zipper. Color ranges from white to patterned prints. When uncompressed, maintains a lofted thickness of 10-20 cm. Distinguishing features include rectangular cushion geometry, fabric casing with visible stitching, and compressible soft form.

Lightweight hollow sphere used in table tennis, constructed from celluloid or ABS plastic with a diameter of exactly 40 mm. Surface is matte or semi-gloss white or orange with a visible seam line encircling the equator where two hemispherical halves are joined. Material is thin-walled (approximately 0.4 mm), producing a characteristic hollow sound when struck. Weight is 2.7 grams. Surface may bear printed brand markings, star ratings (1-3 stars), or ITTF certification logos. Highly reflective under direct light due to smooth plastic finish. Distinguishing features include precise 40 mm spherical geometry, equatorial seam line, and lightweight hollow construction.

Decorative wind-driven toy consisting of a central hub with multiple colored vanes or blades arranged radially around a pivot point. Vanes are typically triangular or curved, constructed from lightweight plastic, paper, or thin metal, measuring 5-15 cm in diameter overall. Each vane is angled to catch wind, causing the assembly to rotate around a central pin or axle. Mounted on a slender stick or handle (20-50 cm long) made of wood or plastic. Vanes display alternating bright colors (red, blue, yellow, green) creating a spinning color wheel effect when in motion. Distinguishing features include radial blade arrangement, central pivot axis, and wind-driven rotational mechanism.

Historical sailing vessel associated with maritime piracy, typically a multi-masted wooden ship with square-rigged sails. Hull constructed from dark-stained timber planking with visible caulking seams between boards. Features two or three masts (fore, main, and mizzen) with canvas sails, rigging lines, and yardarms. Deck includes a raised sterncastle and forecastle, cannons protruding from gun ports along the hull sides, and a bowsprit extending forward. Flag displays the Jolly Roger (skull and crossbones) or similar pirate ensign on a black background. Overall length 30-50 meters. Distinguishing features include cannon armament, black pirate flag, multi-masted square rig configuration, and weathered wooden hull appearance.

Open-top liquid serving vessel with a cylindrical or bulbous body, a pouring spout, and a C-shaped handle attached to the opposite side. Capacity ranges from 0.5 to 2.0 liters. Constructed from glass, ceramic, stainless steel, or plastic. Glass variants are transparent with smooth curved surfaces; ceramic variants feature glazed finishes in solid colors or decorative patterns. Spout is an integrated extension of the rim, tapered for controlled pouring. Handle arcs from upper rim to mid-body for ergonomic grip. Height ranges from 15-30 cm. Distinguishing features include open top (no lid), single pouring spout, opposing handle attachment, and liquid-serving proportions.

Woodworking hand tool consisting of a solid metal or wooden body (sole) with an adjustable cutting blade mounted at an angle through a slot. Body is rectangular block-shaped, 20-35 cm in length, with a flat bottom surface (sole) that rides against the wood being worked. Blade protrudes slightly through a mouth opening in the sole, shaving thin layers of wood as the tool is pushed forward. Adjustment mechanism includes a lever cap, lateral adjustment lever, and depth-adjustment wheel. Front knob and rear handle provide two-handed grip. Constructed from cast iron, steel, or hardwood with polished or patinated finish. Distinguishing features include flat sole surface, angled blade exposure, dual-handle configuration, and wood-shaving function.

Specialized building housing a projection theater for astronomical education, characterized by a prominent dome-shaped roof structure. Exterior features a circular or polygonal base supporting a hemispherical dome constructed from concrete, metal panels, or geodesic framework. Dome diameter ranges from 10 to 30 meters. Entrance typically includes a lobby area with ticketing and exhibition space. Interior contains a central projection instrument (star projector) surrounded by tiered seating arranged in concentric circles facing upward toward the domed ceiling. Ceiling surface is smooth, white, or perforated for acoustic optimization. Distinguishing features include hemispherical dome silhouette, circular floor plan, and institutional science-education architecture.

Flexible container manufactured from thin polyethylene film (LDPE or HDPE), typically transparent, translucent, or printed with branding. Thickness ranges from 0.01 to 0.05 mm, creating a crinkly, lightweight material that conforms to contents. Common configurations include T-shirt bags with integrated handles, flat pouch bags with heat-sealed edges, and zip-lock bags with interlocking closure strips. Dimensions vary from small produce bags (15 x 20 cm) to large shopping bags (40 x 50 cm). Surface exhibits characteristic wrinkles, folds, and light refraction patterns. Handles may be die-cut loops or attached loops. Distinguishing features include thin flexible film material, translucent appearance, and characteristic crinkled texture.

Kitchen drying rack constructed from wire, wood, or stainless steel, designed to hold plates vertically for air drying. Frame consists of parallel vertical slots or grooves spaced 2-4 cm apart to accommodate individual plates, mounted within a rectangular framework. Dimensions approximately 30-60 cm wide, 25-40 cm tall, and 20-30 cm deep. Base includes a drip tray or open drainage area. Wire variants feature chrome-plated or powder-coated metal rods bent into plate-holding configuration. Wooden variants have slotted boards with routed grooves. May include additional tiers or shelves for cups and utensils. Distinguishing features include vertical plate slot arrangement, drainage-oriented design, and compact kitchen counter footprint.
